ai.title: Simplify Gravity ads client and add request logging
ai.summary: Refactored `useGravityAd` to remove pre-fetch logic, simplifying rotation to a single 60-second interval (`AD_ROTATION_INTERVAL_MS`) and gating ad display behind user activity. Updated `postAds` to authenticate before parsing the request body, filter empty messages, and log the full request payload for debugging. Added `userId` and `operationId` to impression pixel logs in `postAdImpression` for better traceability. Covers `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` and `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/`.

eli5.text: Ads in the assistant now only appear after you've sent your first message, rather than loading automatically in the background before then. Each ad still shows for one minute, but the system no longer pre-loads the next one early, which means swaps happen on a simpler 60-second cycle tied to your activity. The server side is more careful now: it checks your login before accepting the ad request, ignores any messages with no content, and records the full request details for troubleshooting. When an ad's tracking pixel fires, that log line now includes who you are and which task you're working on, so support can trace problems back to you more easily.

ai.title: Tighten context pruner summary target to 10 percent
ai.summary: Context pruner target summary factor drops from 15% to 10% of max context. User message truncation limit lowers to 15000 chars; assistant limit to 4000. Affects .agents/context-pruner.ts. Formatting tweaks in findLastIndex and splice logic.

eli5.text: The system that keeps conversation histories tidy is now trimming them sooner: it holds onto roughly 10% of the maximum space for summarized messages instead of 15%, and it clips very long messages a bit tighter (user messages above about 15,000 characters and assistant replies above 4,000 are cut). If you were watching the logs, you'd see summaries shrinking and long past messages getting trimmed a little harder around the edges, with a couple of tiny formatting cleanups in how those trims are applied. This tightening is live today for anyone using the agent with built-in context pruning.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.569 released with pruner, agent, ad, and CLI perf updates
ai.summary: Version 1.0.569 bundles the same-day sequence of user-visible work on context pruning, agent prompting, Gravity ads, and CLI rendering. The context-pruner now strips think tags, targets 10% of max context for summaries (down from 15%), truncates user and assistant messages to 15000 and 4000 chars respectively before summarization, and prunes on 5-minute prompt-cache expiry using sentAt timestamps stripped before transmission. The base2 agent gates think-tag instructions to default and max modes, includes ask_user as a workflow step unless noAskUser is set, and switches the isOpus flag from hardcoded true to !isLite. Gravity ad handling simplifies to a single 60-second rotation, authenticates before parsing, filters empty messages, logs full request payloads, and tags impression pixels with userId and operationId. CLI rendering gains a CODEBUFF_PERF_TEST env flag gating useWhyDidYouUpdateById logging in AgentBranchItem and MessageBlock, complementing the useMemo-stabilized streamingAgents reference and useCallback-memoized onOpenFeedback that prevent unnecessary re-renders.
ai.evidence: Commit 5c3aab08 modifies only cli/release/package.json, changing the version field from 1.0.568 to 1.0.569 with a single +/- line. The surrounding same-day commit sequence provides the user-visible changes that this release bump aggregates: context-pruner simplifications (10% summary factor, 20000/5000 char pre-summarization truncation tightened to 15000/4000), think-tag stripping, 5-minute cache-expiry pruning trigger with sentAt timestamps, Anthropic token-count proxying replacing local

eli5.text: This release makes Freebuff faster, smarter, and more reliable for your coding sessions. First, the built-in help feature now actively asks you clarifying questions when it senses confusion, instead of sitting silently and guessing what you need. Second, a new context-compression system replaces old heuristic trimming with a single-pass AI summarization that condenses long conversations into a concise summary, keeping your most important details intact while dropping the filler. Third, the command-line interface loads and scrolls more smoothly, thanks to fixes that stop unnecessary screen redraws and add a secret developer switch to debug any future slowdowns. Fourth, a new performance-testing mode and smarter test tools help the team catch and fix sluggishness before you ever notice it. Together, these changes mean faster prompts, cleaner summaries of long chats, and a UI that feels snappier every day you use it.

ai.title: Skip empty text parts in Anthropic message conversion
ai.summary: The `convertContentToAnthropic` function in `web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts` now filters out empty or whitespace-only text parts before adding them to the Anthropic message payload. Previously, trimmed empty strings were pushed as `type: 'text'` content blocks, which could cause validation errors or unexpected behavior in the Anthropic API. This change ensures only non-empty text content is included in the converted messages.

eli5.text: When the system talks to the AI assistant behind the scenes, it now skips over any empty or blank messages it used to include by accident. Before, harmless empty spaces in text could cause the assistant to get confused or send back an error. You wouldn't notice this unless an assistant message was missing or failing to process, and it's already live now.

ai.title: CLI and agent runtime migrate live user input checks to AbortSignal
ai.summary: Replaced custom `liveUserInputRecord` and `sessionConnections` state with standard `AbortSignal` for cancellation. `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` now passes `abortController.signal` into `createRunConfig`, which threads it through `packages/agent-runtime/src/main-prompt.ts` and `prompt-agent-stream.ts`. Deleted `packages/agent-runtime/src/live-user-inputs.ts` and `common/src/types/contracts/live-user-input.ts`, updating type contracts in `common/src/types/contracts/llm.ts` to require `signal: AbortSignal` instead of check functions. Evals in `evals/impl/agent-runtime.ts` and `evals/buffbench/pick-commits.ts` updated to provide dummy signals, removing reliance on `disableLiveUserInputCheck`.

eli5.text: When you type a message to the assistant in the command-line tool, the system used to run a custom check in the background to decide whether to stop or let your message through. That custom check, along with its supporting bookkeeping about your session, has been removed entirely; instead, the program now relies on a built-in web-standard cancel mechanism (AbortSignal) to handle stopping mid-response. If you look, you won't see a visible difference while chatting today, but behind the scenes the code that handled your typing is much simpler and is being phased in across the CLI and agent components, with supporting files already deleted and type definitions updated to expect the new cancel signal rather than the old manual check functions.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.570 release bundles AbortSignal live-input migration
ai.summary: Version 1.0.570 is a release-only bump in `cli/release/package.json`, rolling up two features that shipped since 1.0.569. The live user-input cancellation path in the agent runtime and CLI (`cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`) now threads a standard `AbortSignal` through `createRunConfig` into `main-prompt.ts` and `prompt-agent-stream.ts`, deleting `live-user-inputs.ts` and `live-user-input.ts` and requiring `signal: AbortSignal` in the `llm.ts` contract. The Anthropic token-count endpoint (`web/src/app/api/v1/token-count/_post.ts`) now filters empty or whitespace-only text parts before emitting them as `type: 'text'` blocks to avoid Anthropic API validation errors. Both changes are user-visible across Web, CLI, and Desktop via the same release package.
ai.evidence: Commit 965b1e6f bumps the version in `cli/release/package.json` from 1.0.569 to 1.0.570 with a single-line +1/-1 change, constituting the release-bump for the 1.0.570 release.

eli5.text: This release improves how Freebuff handles live user input and message handling, making the CLI more reliable and stable. The main change replaces older custom tracking systems for live user input with a standard web-based cancellation mechanism called AbortSignal, which means stopping or interrupting an ongoing task in the terminal now works more predictably and consistently. When you type a message while Freebuff is thinking, the system now cleanly cancels the current response instead of potentially getting confused or leaving background processes hanging. Additionally, the token counting feature now filters out empty or blank text when preparing messages for certain AI models, preventing validation errors and ensuring smoother interactions. Upgrading gives you a more stable experience when interrupting or taking control during AI conversations, with fewer errors and cleaner handling of live typing. The CLI's core loop is also slightly faster and more dependable thanks to these under-the-hood improvements.

ai.title: Block banned users from buying credits
ai.summary: Added `banned` column checks to credit purchase routes in `web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/credits/route.ts` and `web/src/app/api/stripe/buy-credits/route.ts`. Prevents suspended accounts from purchasing credits by returning 403 errors and logging warnings. Scope limited to Web API routes.

eli5.text: If you try to buy credits while your account is suspended, the system now stops you and shows an "account suspended" message, then logs the attempt. You'll see this whether you're buying credits directly through Stripe or requesting them for a specific organization. Only accounts flagged as banned are affected, and the restriction applies in both purchase paths on the web.

ai.title: Gravity ad request message assembly fixes
ai.summary: The `useGravityAd` hook now wraps the latest UI user message in `<user_message>` tags and checks for substring containment before appending, preventing duplicate or missing context in ad requests. `convertToAdMessages` updated to filter out `INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT` tags instead of `USER_PROMPT`. This ensures system instructions are excluded from gravity ad payloads while preserving user context. Scope limited to `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question, it now wraps your latest message in special tags and double-checks whether it's already sent that exact message before including it again, so gravity ad requests receive one clear user message instead of duplicated or missing context. The system also now filters out internal instruction tags rather than prompt tags when converting messages, ensuring only your conversation context (not system instructions) gets forwarded to gravity ads. These corrections are live today and only affect gravity ad message assembly.

ai.title: Version 1.0.571 bumps CLI release package
ai.summary: The release package.json for the CLI bumps from version 1.0.570 to 1.0.571, capturing two minor changes since the prior release. This release blocks banned users from buying credits by checking the new `banned` column in the Web API credit routes (`web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/credits/route.ts` and `web/src/app/api/stripe/buy-credits/route.ts`) and returning 403. It also fixes the gravity ad request message assembly in the `useGravityAd` hook (`cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`), which now wraps the latest user message in `<user_message>` tags and filters `INSTRUCTIONS_PROMPT` tags instead of `USER_PROMPT` to prevent duplicate or missing context in ad payloads.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json increments the version field from 1.0.570 to 1.0.571.

eli5.text: This release adds new safeguards to stop banned users from buying credits, and improves how ads are displayed so they show the right context without duplicates. Suspended accounts can no longer purchase credits through the web interface, and the ad system now wraps your latest message in proper tags and skips system instructions so sponsored content matches what you're actually working on. Upgrading means better security around account access and cleaner, more relevant ad placement that reflects your real task instead of hidden system prompts. The billing guardrails also log warnings when someone tries to buy credits while banned, giving administrators clearer visibility into blocked purchase attempts.
